disposition.reason: The only candidate whose resolution changes something for two active lines at once (period collapse and Littlewood-Richardson positivity) and whose evidence is structural (a theorem of period collapse plus a census of necessary conditions) rather than a pattern.

neighbours: Ehrhart form: for every admissible triple there is a lattice polytope $Q$ with $L_Q(t)=c^{t\nu}_{t\lambda,t\mu}$.
Haase-McAllister form: $H(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ is $\mathrm{GL}_D(\mathbb{Z})$-equidecomposable with a disjoint union of integral open simplices (their Conjecture 3.2 restricted to hive polytopes).
Gelfand-Tsetlin sibling: the Gelfand-Tsetlin polytope $GT(\lambda,\mu)$ of a Kostka number is $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb{Z})$-equidecomposable with a lattice polytope.
Consequence: the numerator $G^{\nu}_{\lambda\mu}(z)$ of $\sum_t c^{t\nu}_{t\lambda,t\mu}z^t$ has nonnegative coefficients (the second King-Tollu-Toumazet conjecture of 2004).
Rank restriction: the statement for partitions of length at most $r$; for $r\le 4$ every hive polytope is a lattice polytope (Buch), so the first open rank is $r=5$.
notes: Grade what the question would be if it holds: a positive answer is the first polyhedral explanation of the period collapse of hive polytopes, the motivating open case of Haase-McAllister's conjecture, and it implies the h*-positivity conjecture of King-Tollu-Toumazet; a negative answer identifies a representation-theoretic family whose period collapse is not explained by rearrangement into one lattice polytope, which would sharpen Haase-McAllister's Example 2.4 from an ad hoc quadrilateral to a structured family. The strongest objection is that the statement is a special case of a known conjecture; it is not: Haase-McAllister ask for a union of open simplices and show the single-polytope form fails in general, so the single-polytope form for hives is strictly sharper and is supported by evidence that the general form cannot have.
observation: Every one of the 6,855,302 certified hive polynomials (five, six and seven parts, size at most 30, denominators up to 6) has an h*-vector satisfying the five inequalities that the h*-vector of a lattice polytope must satisfy (nonnegativity, interior bound, Hibi's lower bound, Stanley's inequality, Hibi's 1990 inequality), and every one of the 52,671 two-dimensional hive polytopes of at most five parts and size at most 22 has the Ehrhart polynomial of a lattice polygon (b >= 3 and Scott's inequality), although Haase-McAllister's Example 2.4 and Bohnert's classification show that rational polytopes with period collapse in general do not. The period collapse of hive polytopes is a theorem (Derksen-Weyman, Rassart, Thawinrak) with no polyhedral proof, which is exactly the gap Haase-McAllister's conjecture names; a single-lattice-polytope equidecomposition would give that proof and would imply the second King-Tollu-Toumazet conjecture (nonnegative integer coefficients of the generating-function numerator G(z)) through Stanley's nonnegativity.
